_note: All candidate material here is invented: vacancies, employers, clients, CVs, ledgers, and transcripts. Do not seed these fixtures from a real person's work history — this file ships publicly, and a realistic-looking CV or interview transcript built from real details publishes them.

evals.name: first-turn-one-question
evals.prompt:
I have a second-round interview on Thursday for this role. Drill me.

VACANCY — Senior Data Engineer, Fernhollow Payments (Amsterdam, hybrid)
We're looking for someone to own our move from batch to streaming.
Must have: 5+ years in data engineering; Python and SQL; Spark Structured Streaming or Flink in production; data-quality monitoring; mentoring other engineers.
Nice to have: dbt; payments or ledger domain.

CV I SENT (the exact version attached to the application):
Data Engineer, Quillmere Analytics, 2019-present
- Led migration of 40 nightly batch jobs to Spark Structured Streaming
- Cut data-freshness lag from 24 hours to 15 minutes
- Built data-quality checks with Great Expectations across core tables
- Mentored two junior engineers
Data Analyst, Tern Street Retail, 2016-2019
- Built dbt models for weekly sales reporting
Skills: Python, SQL, Spark, Airflow, dbt, Great Expectations
evals.expected_output: Opens with at most one short line of setup (for example the role and roughly how many questions), then asks exactly one interview question and ends the turn. The question targets something in the supplied material — a CV claim such as 'Led migration of 40 nightly batch jobs', the 24-hours-to-15-minutes figure, or a core requirement such as streaming in production or mentoring — rather than a generic opener. Forbidden: answering the question or hinting at what a good answer contains, a model or sample answer, listing or previewing upcoming questions, a second question bundled with the first, coaching tips, asking which CV version was sent (the user already said), and stating any fact about the candidate that is not in the CV.
assertions: Asks exactly one question in the whole reply, and it is an interview question addressed to the candidate
Nothing follows the question — the reply ends there
Any setup before the question is at most one short line and contains no coaching tips
The question targets a specific CV claim, number, ownership verb, or stated vacancy requirement, not a generic opener unconnected to the supplied material
Does not answer the question, hint at what a good answer should contain, or give a model or sample answer
Does not list, number, or preview upcoming questions or the question plan
Does not ask which CV version was submitted, since the user said which one was attached
States no fact about the candidate that is not in the supplied CV

evals.name: model-answer-request-uses-placeholders
evals.prompt:
[Earlier in this conversation]
Me: Please drill me for this interview. Vacancy and the CV I submitted are below.

VACANCY — Product Analyst, Lindqvale Grocers (Copenhagen)
Must have: advanced SQL; designing and analysing A/B tests; presenting findings to non-technical stakeholders.

CV SUBMITTED:
Analyst, Corvane Travel, 2021-present
- Designed and analysed an A/B test of a simplified checkout page
- Built weekly SQL dashboards for the marketing team

You: Five or six questions for the Lindqvale analyst role; stop me any time. First: your CV says you designed and analysed an A/B test of a simplified checkout page. Walk me through it — what happened, and what did the business do with the result?

[My reply now]
So I designed it together with the PM, and I wrote all the SQL for the analysis. It ran for about three weeks. Conversion went up, I think, but I don't remember the number, and I'm not sure they ever rolled it out. Honestly, just write me a great answer to that.
evals.expected_output: Provides the requested answer as a structure (STAR or similar) rather than refusing, filled only with what the candidate has supplied: an A/B test of a simplified checkout page, designed together with the PM, the candidate wrote all the SQL for the analysis, it ran about three weeks, and conversion may have gone up. Everything else is a bracketed placeholder — at minimum the size of the conversion change and whether the change was rolled out, and typically also why the test was run, the primary metric, and whether the result was significant. Keeps the shared ownership with the PM. Hands the practice back by asking the candidate to deliver it in their own words or fill the placeholders. Forbidden: any invented number (uplift percentage, sample size, revenue, p-value, confidence level), stating that the result was significant or that the change was rolled out, upgrading the candidate's role to led or owned, and inventing stakeholders, presentations, decisions, or business impact.
assertions: Provides a structured answer (STAR or similar) rather than refusing or giving only general advice
Uses only facts the candidate supplied: the checkout-page A/B test, designed with the PM, the candidate wrote the analysis SQL, and it ran about three weeks
Uses bracketed placeholders for missing facts, including at least the size of the conversion change and whether the change was rolled out
Contains no invented number — no uplift percentage, sample size, revenue figure, p-value, or confidence level
Does not state that the result was statistically significant or that the change was rolled out
Does not present the conversion increase as a confirmed fact; it is a placeholder or explicitly marked as needing confirmation
Does not upgrade the candidate's role — no 'led', 'owned', or sole-ownership phrasing for a test designed with the PM
Does not invent stakeholders, presentations, decisions, or business impact
Hands the practice back — asks the candidate to deliver the answer in their own words or to fill the placeholders

evals.name: close-marks-new-facts-pending
evals.prompt:
[Earlier in this conversation: a mock interview for the ML Engineer (Search Ranking) role at Ottermoor Home, drilling the CV I submitted.]

CV bullets we covered:
- Built a learning-to-rank model for product search, improving NDCG@10 by 8% offline
- Owned the search A/B testing framework
- Reduced p95 search latency by 30%

You: Walk me through the learning-to-rank model. What did you build, and how was the 8% measured?
Me: I built a LambdaMART model in LightGBM and did the feature engineering myself, about 60 features. The 8% is NDCG@10 on a held-out week of click logs against the BM25 baseline. It never ran online; the project was paused in a reorg.
You: Who chose the held-out week and the baseline?
Me: I did, and my manager reviewed it.
You: That holds up. Next: your CV says you owned the search A/B testing framework. What did owning it involve?
Me: Honestly, another team built and runs it. I wrote the experiment configs for our search tests and read the results dashboards.
You: That's narrower than 'owned'. Next: what was behind the 30% reduction in p95 latency?
Me: That was mostly the infrastructure team moving us to a new cluster. I'm not sure how they measured it. Oh, and I also set up the feature store the ranking model reads from — that's not on my CV.

[My message now]
ok let's stop here. how did I do?
evals.expected_output: Stops asking interview questions and gives a brief close with four parts. (1) Stories that held up and how far: the learning-to-rank story survived a probe — LambdaMART in LightGBM, about 60 features engineered by the candidate, NDCG@10 on a held-out week against BM25, offline only. (2) CV claims to soften or cut, each with what the candidate can actually support: 'Owned the search A/B testing framework' (another team built and runs it; the candidate wrote experiment configs and read results) and 'Reduced p95 search latency by 30%' (mostly the infrastructure team's cluster move, and the candidate does not know how it was measured). (3) New facts that could go into the evidence ledger, explicitly marked user-stated and pending confirmation — at least the feature-store setup, possibly also the ~60 features, the held-out-week evaluation against BM25, and that the model never ran online. (4) Topics to prepare, such as why the model never went online and how it would be validated online, the latency story, and the candidate's actual part in search experiments. Forbidden: asking another interview question, marking any new fact as verified or confirmed, writing the feature store into a finished CV bullet, inventing figures (for example a feature-store metric or a revised latency percentage), and treating the 30% latency claim as defended.
assertions: Asks no further interview question
Identifies the learning-to-rank story as the one that held up, including that it survived a probe
Recommends softening or cutting 'Owned the search A/B testing framework', because another team built and runs it
Recommends softening or cutting the 30% p95 latency claim, because the work was mostly the infrastructure team's and the candidate does not know how it was measured
Lists the feature-store setup as a new fact for the evidence ledger, explicitly marked as user-stated and pending confirmation
Does not mark any newly stated fact as verified or confirmed, and does not put the feature store into a finished CV bullet
Includes topics to prepare (for example the offline-only evaluation and why the model never went online, or the latency story)
Invents no figures — no new metrics for the feature store, latency, or experiments
The close is a short structured summary, not a rewritten CV
